<div class="nv-rule" id="echo-always-has-a-sink">

## Every execution context binds `echo` to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#echo-always-has-a-sink"><code>tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink</code></a>
</div>

| Context | `echo` writes to | Carrier |
|---|---|---|
| an HTTP request | the response body | `Core\Html\Markup`, auto-escaping ([`core-classes/html-auto-escape`](/docs/rules/core-classes/regex-html-and-introspection/#html-auto-escape "echo in an HTTP request escapes everything it is given, and Core\Html\Markup is the only raw-write bypass")) |
| a CLI program — a `#[Command]` method or a script's main task | stdout | `Cli\Text`, substituting ([`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink "Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty")) |
| a `spawn script` isolate | its own output buffer, or the parent's stream under `output: 'inherit'` | the parent's carrier ([`security/isolate-output-is-captured`](/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-output-is-captured "An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier")) |
| a scheduled script, a job worker, a `#[Test]` method | that run's captured output | `Cli\Text` |
| a connection isolate, from either `upgrade` door | that connection's captured output | `Cli\Text` |

**A connection isolate takes the default sink because it is not a request.** The request that
upgraded it ended ([`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-root-isolate`](/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-connection-is-a-root-isolate "A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends")), so nothing attaches the HTML
sink to the root that replaced it, and a socket connection and an event-stream connection are one row
rather than two — the door decides what the program may do, never where its `echo` lands
([`concurrency/two-doors-one-isolate`](/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#two-doors-one-isolate "Core\Socket and Core\Sse are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing")). A request that answers with a *streamed* body is the
opposite case and stays on row one: it is still an HTTP request, so the HTML sink is still attached,
and `echo` beside the member writing that body does not compile
([`security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`](/docs/rules/security/laundering/#response-body-is-one-typed-member "A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing echo with one of them does not compile")).

**The terminal sink is the default; the HTML sink is attached by an HTTP request and by nothing
else.** That is the fail-closed direction, for the terminal sink's own reason: its substitution is
uniform rather than tty-dependent precisely because a CI log is written to a pipe and read by a human
later, which is exactly what a scheduled run's and a job worker's output is. A context with no
attached sink does not exist, so `echo` never has an undefined meaning — and where the meaning had to
be chosen, it was chosen to neutralize. Routing a sinkless context's `echo` to `Core\Log` instead was
rejected: it silently reshapes free text into the structured writer.

The same table selects a rendering ([`errors/renderings`](/docs/rules/errors/diagnostics-and-logging/#renderings "The sink in force picks the rendering, and no call site may name one")): the sink in force decides not only
where a log record, a dump, a trace or a diagnostic goes but whether it is drawn as plaintext, JSON or
HTML, so no call site names a format. It also gives `Core\Out::capture` its answer
([`security/capture-answers-the-carrier`](/docs/rules/security/laundering/#capture-answers-the-carrier "Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain string")), and it is why a JSON body is `Response::json` rather
than an `echo` the HTML sink would escape into corruption
([`security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`](/docs/rules/security/laundering/#response-body-is-one-typed-member "A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing echo with one of them does not compile")).

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>echo</code> in a scheduled script, a job worker or a test neutralizes control bytes rather than writing raw, and only an HTTP request makes it HTML</p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="terminal-output-is-a-sink">

## Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#terminal-output-is-a-sink"><code>tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink</code></a>
</div>

Standard output and standard error are sinks. Every value written through `echo` or `Cli::write` —
**regardless of qualifier** — has its control bytes replaced before a byte reaches the stream: `LF`
and `TAB` pass through; every other C0 byte, `ESC` and `CR` included, becomes its U+2400 Control
Picture (`ESC` → `␛`, `CR` → `␍`); `DEL` becomes `␡`; a C1 code point becomes `�`; an unterminated
bidirectional control becomes `�` while a balanced one passes ([`security/bidi-predicate`](/docs/rules/security/bidi-and-passwords/#bidi-predicate "A span is rejected when it ends with a directional scope still open, decided by two counters")). Twelve
terminal CVEs in 2022–23 were reached through exactly the output `git`, `less` and `kubectl` print.

The rule is **uniform**. It does not depend on whether the value is `tainted`, because that would make
*whether output is escaped* hinge on a fact invisible at the `echo` line; and it does not depend on
whether the stream is a terminal, because a CI log is written to a pipe and read by a human later.
Styling is tty-dependent ([`tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once "The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling")); neutralizing never is.
In one sentence: **`echo` prints text. `Core\Cli\Text` prints terminal commands.**

Unlike HTML's `&` → `&amp;`, this transforms no visible text: a control sequence was never text, and
today those bytes vanish into the terminal's command stream unseen. Substituting makes `echo` show
*more* of what arrived, and nothing is silently dropped. `Core\Cli::escape(tainted string): string`
is the sink's named launderer, performing exactly this table, for the program that wants the
neutralized form as a value. A `secret` value is refused outright with no carrier bypass
([`security/secret-sinks-refuse`](/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-sinks-refuse "Every output sink refuses a secret value outright, and no auto-escape or neutralisation bypasses one")), because substitution does nothing for confidentiality.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>echo &quot;\e[31m&quot;</code> prints <code>␛[31m</code> rather than turning the text red, on a pipe and a terminal alike; colour is <code>Core\Cli\Text</code></p>
</aside>

<div class="nv-rule" id="text-is-the-one-raw-path">

## `Cli\Text` is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#text-is-the-one-raw-path"><code>tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path</code></a>
</div>

`Cli\Text` is peer to `Core\Html\Markup` and the only value the terminal sink writes raw. Its two
constructors, `Text::plain(string)` and `Text::styled(string, Style)`, **both apply the sink's
substitution to their input**, so the only control bytes a `Text` can carry are the ones its `Style`
put there. That is the structural guarantee: `Text` is not a trust assertion a developer can be
tricked into making, it is a constructor that cannot produce an injected sequence. `Text + Text` is
`Text`, immutable, composing the way `Markup + Markup` does, and `Text::plain` is idempotent, so text
that has already been through the sink is never escaped twice.

A `Text` holds bytes, so the styling is rendered when it is built, against the profile resolved once
for the process ([`tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once "The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling")), not at the write. The known
limit: a `Text` written to a terminal standard output and to a redirected standard error in one run
sends both the same bytes. Closing it would make the sink's carrier
([`security/capture-answers-the-carrier`](/docs/rules/security/laundering/#capture-answers-the-carrier "Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain string")) two representations instead of one, and that trade is
not worth making while `echo` writes standard output and nothing else can observe the difference.

<div class="nv-rule" id="an-escape-in-a-literal-is-a-compile-error">

## An `ESC` in a source literal is a compile error that names `Core\Cli\Text`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#an-escape-in-a-literal-is-a-compile-error"><code>tooling/an-escape-in-a-literal-is-a-compile-error</code></a>
</div>

An `ESC` byte in a source literal is a compile error naming the site and the fix: *raw terminal
escapes are not how output is styled — use `Core\Cli\Text`.*

This is what keeps [`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink "Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty") from being a trap. A program whose
literals hold no `ESC` — every program that does not hand-roll colour — is byte-identical with the
sink in place, and the one program that would be surprised by `␛[31m` on its screen is told at compile
time, at the exact line. With the literal case closed, the only way to meet the substitution at run
time is to print a **computed** escape sequence, which is the attack the sink exists to neutralize.
The diagnostic names `Cli\Text` so that a developer who wants colour finds the one raw path
([`tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#text-is-the-one-raw-path "Cli\Text is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input")) instead of concluding that colour does not work.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A hand-rolled <code>&quot;\e[1m&quot;</code> literal fails the build instead of styling the output</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink" title="Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty"><code>tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#text-is-the-one-raw-path" title="Cli\Text is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input"><code>tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar">

## Styling is a value type — `Cli\Style` and `Cli\Color` — and never a fifth grammar

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar"><code>tooling/styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar</code></a>
</div>

The library's grammar count is fixed at four — a regex pattern, a `printf` template, a CLDR date
pattern and a `pack` format ([`core-api/shape-rules`](/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#shape-rules "Every Core member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20") R11, each a sink under
[`security/every-grammar-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#every-grammar-is-a-sink "Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer")). Both obvious styling designs would be a fifth: raw
`"\e[31m"` escapes, and a `"<red>…</red>"` markup string, which would also collide with the
inline-HTML lexer mode. So styling is typed values, and the count stays four.

```nvs
var $warn = Cli\Style::of({color: Cli\Color::YELLOW, bold: true});
Cli::write(Cli\Text::styled("deleting ", $warn) + Cli\Text::plain($path));
```

`Cli\Style::of({color?, background?, bold?, dim?, italic?, underline?, strikethrough?})` is the one
trailing shape. **`Cli\Color` is a value type, not an enum**: a closed named integer type
([`enums/closed-integer-type`](/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type "An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type")) does not fit a set with sixteen million members. The sixteen named
colours are class constants — `Color::RED` *is* `Color::index(1)`, written shorter, inlined at every
use site as any scalar constant is — and `Color::rgb(uint, uint, uint)` and `Color::index(uint)`
construct the rest.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>There is no escape string and no <code>&lt;red&gt;…&lt;/red&gt;</code> markup; a style is <code>Cli\Style::of({...})</code> over <code>Cli\Color</code> values</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#text-is-the-one-raw-path" title="Cli\Text is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input"><code>tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once" title="The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling"><code>tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/tainted-data/#every-grammar-is-a-sink" title="Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer"><code>security/every-grammar-is-a-sink</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/naming-and-shape/#shape-rules" title="Every Core member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20"><code>core-api/shape-rules</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/enums/#closed-integer-type" title="An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type"><code>enums/closed-integer-type</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-the-sixteen-named-colours-are-class-constants.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-the-sixteen-named-colours-are-class-constants.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-a-styles-seven-slots-are-independent.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-a-styles-seven-slots-are-independent.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-terminal-profile-resolves-once">

## The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once"><code>tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once</code></a>
</div>

Whether each standard stream is a terminal, the colour depth — honouring `NO_COLOR`,
`CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb`, and enabling Windows virtual terminal processing
where it exists — and the width and height are **resolved once per process, not per call**.
`Cli::isTty(Cli\Stream)`, `Cli::width()`, `Cli::height()` and `Cli::colorDepth()` read that profile;
`80`/`24` is the answer when there is no controlling terminal. `Cli\Stream` is an enum of `In`, `Out`
and `Err`, because "is a tty" is always a question about one stream and *colour on stdout while stdin
is a pipe* is the common case a single `isTty()` cannot express.

A program never asks what the terminal supports. It writes `Cli\Text`, and styling degrades truecolor
→ 256 → 16 → none against the profile. **When the stream is not a terminal, styling is dropped
entirely**, so `myprog | grep` and a CI log are plain — while the control-byte substitution of
[`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink "Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty") still applies, because that is a safety rule and not a
presentation one. Resolving once is what makes two reads of the width in one run the same number by
construction, so a program that measures at the top and draws at the bottom cannot tear a frame; the
cost is that a resize is not noticed until the process restarts.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>posix_isatty</code>, <code>NO_COLOR</code> handling and <code>tput cols</code> are one profile read at start-up; a program writes <code>Cli\Text</code> and never asks what the terminal supports</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar" title="Styling is a value type — Cli\Style and Cli\Color — and never a fifth grammar"><code>tooling/styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes" title="Cli::displayWidth measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns"><code>tooling/display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink" title="Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty"><code>tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-the-terminal-profile-resolves-once-per-process.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-the-terminal-profile-resolves-once-per-process.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-a-stream-that-is-no-terminal-shows-no-colour.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-a-stream-that-is-no-terminal-shows-no-colour.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-a-process-with-no-terminal-measures-eighty-by-twenty-four.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-a-process-with-no-terminal-measures-eighty-by-twenty-four.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes">

## `Cli::displayWidth` measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes"><code>tooling/display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes</code></a>
</div>

`Cli::displayWidth(string): uint` answers UAX #11 terminal columns for **the string the sink will
write, not the one it was handed**. The substitution of [`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink "Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty") is
applied first, so a control byte costs what its Control Picture costs — one column, never zero — and a
value cannot shrink its own measured width by carrying an escape sequence, which is what makes the
answer safe to lay a box out against.

The count is over grapheme clusters: a combining mark is no column of its own and an emoji ZWJ
sequence is one pair however many code points built it, where summing code points misaligns exactly
the table this member is asked for. The two code points the sink passes through are the two that are
not columns: `TAB` advances to the next multiple of eight, so its cost depends on where it stands, and
`LF` ends the row, so a value spanning several rows answers the width of its *widest* one — the
number a box is padded to.

It lives on `Core\Cli` and not on `Core\Str` deliberately. A column count is a third measure beside
the two [`types/bytes`](/docs/rules/types/text-and-literal-types/#bytes "bytes is a primitive peer to string for data that carries no encoding") fixed — bytes for `bytes`, grapheme clusters for `string` — and it is a
property of the renderer, not of the string; putting it on `Core\Str` would imply a string has an
intrinsic width, the confusion [`types/string-is-utf8`](/docs/rules/types/text-and-literal-types/#string-is-utf8 "A string is valid UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, and its unmarked unit is the grapheme cluster") exists to remove.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>mb_strwidth</code> counts code points and sees an escape sequence as zero columns; <code>displayWidth</code> counts the substituted string, so a control byte costs one column</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once" title="The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling"><code>tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink" title="Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty"><code>tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/types/text-and-literal-types/#string-is-utf8" title="A string is valid UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, and its unmarked unit is the grapheme cluster"><code>types/string-is-utf8</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/types/text-and-literal-types/#bytes" title="bytes is a primitive peer to string for data that carries no encoding"><code>types/bytes</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-measures-what-the-sink-will-show.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-measures-what-the-sink-will-show.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-tab-reaches-the-stop-and-a-newline-ends-the-row.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-tab-reaches-the-stop-and-a-newline-ends-the-row.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-asks-a-whole-cluster-what-its-code-points-cannot-answer.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-displaywidth-asks-a-whole-cluster-what-its-code-points-cannot-answer.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output">

## There is no raw handle onto standard output or standard error, and no cursor, clipboard or title primitive

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output"><code>tooling/no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output</code></a>
</div>

The terminal's substitution is uniform, so a `Core\IO\File` over descriptor 1 or 2 would not be a
convenience beside the sink — it would be the way around it, available to exactly the computed-escape
case [`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink "Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty") exists to catch. `Cli::write` already *is* writing to
those streams, and no operation is reachable two ways
([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-paradigm-per-operation "No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods")). So the standard-stream surface is `Core\IO::stdin()`
alone, the reading half being neither a sink nor a second spelling of anything. The price, recorded
rather than hidden: a program cannot emit byte-exact binary on its standard output, and one whose
output is bytes names a file.

The same closure keeps four more things out of `Core\Cli`. Cursor primitives, per
[`tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region "In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive"). Reading the clipboard, setting the window
title, or any other `OSC` capability — offering them would re-open, as a feature, the exact channel
the sink closes. Spinners and table rendering, which are pure text composition over `Str::format` and
`displayWidth` and need no terminal privilege, so they are a package's natural first offering rather
than Tier 0 ([`core-api/tier-placement`](/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#tier-placement "A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list")). And a TUI widget layer — panes, focus, event loops —
which is an application framework, not a language surface.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>STDOUT</code>, <code>STDERR</code>, <code>php://stdout</code> and <code>fwrite(STDOUT, …)</code> have no counterpart; byte-exact output names a file, and standard input is <code>Core\IO::stdin()</code> alone</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#terminal-output-is-a-sink" title="Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty"><code>tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#text-is-the-one-raw-path" title="Cli\Text is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input"><code>tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region" title="In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive"><code>tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/one-way-to-do-each-thing/#one-paradigm-per-operation" title="No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods"><code>core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/what-belongs-in-core/#tier-placement" title="A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list"><code>core-api/tier-placement</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0063.md">record 0063</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0051.md">record 0051</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/io-the-standard-streams-are-one-member-and-not-three.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/io-the-standard-streams-are-one-member-and-not-three.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task">

## The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program, so a `Core\Cli` member throws in a request and in a spawned isolate

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task"><code>tooling/the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task</code></a>
</div>

The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program. In a request context and inside a spawned isolate,
every `Core\Cli` member throws: two tasks interleaving escape sequences on one terminal produce output
no one can reason about, and there is no locking scheme that makes it coherent.

**`echo` is not one of those members, and does not throw.** It binds to whatever sink its context has
— the response body under a request, the terminal sink everywhere else, including a scheduled script,
a job worker, a test and a spawned isolate's buffer ([`tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#echo-always-has-a-sink "Every execution context binds echo to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal")). What
throws is claiming the *terminal*; writing text never does. An isolate's `echo` reaches a buffer its
parent owns, never a tty ([`security/isolate-output-is-captured`](/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-output-is-captured "An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier")), which is why the two rules are
consistent rather than in tension.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A request handler cannot reach the terminal at all, where PHP-FPM's <code>STDOUT</code> quietly lands in the server log</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#echo-always-has-a-sink" title="Every execution context binds echo to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal"><code>tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path" title="Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal"><code>tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/isolates/#isolate-output-is-captured" title="An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier"><code>security/isolate-output-is-captured</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-classes/processes-and-files/#cli-arguments" title="Core\Cli::arguments is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth"><code>core-classes/cli-arguments</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0088.md">record 0088</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0006.md">record 0006</a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region">

## In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region"><code>tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region</code></a>
</div>

```nvs
Cli::live(fn($live) => {
    foreach ($files as $f) {
        $live->set([Cli\Text::plain("scanning {$f}")]);
    }
});
```

`Cli::live<T>(callable(Cli\Live): T $body): T` hands its body a `Cli\Live` with `->set(array<Cli\Text> $lines)`;
`Cli::progress<T>(uint $total, callable(Cli\Progress): T $body): T` hands it a `Cli\Progress` with
`->advance({by?: uint, label?: string})`. Both answer what the body computed, at the body's type.
**The runtime owns the cursor**: it coalesces frames on a timer rather than repainting per `set`,
diffs against the previous frame, hides and restores the cursor, and **renders nothing at all when
the stream is not a terminal**, so a piped run produces clean output instead of a smear of escape
sequences. A handle that outlives its region is dead: painting through it is a `LogicError`, because
two regions on one cursor is the state this rule exists to make unreachable.

This is the scoped-closure shape `Out::capture` and `Db::transaction`
([`core-classes/db-transactions`](/docs/rules/core-classes/running-a-statement/#db-transactions "A transaction is a closure, and Transaction is a Queryable rather than a second query surface")) already use, and scoping is what makes restoration enforceable
([`tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path "Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal")): a region has an end, and the runtime is
at that end on every path including a throw. Cursor primitives — `moveUp`, `clearLine`,
`alternateScreen` — are **not** the surface. They break the moment output is piped, they cannot
survive a resize, they interleave incoherently when two tasks write, and a program that dies holding
them leaves the operator's shell unusable.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>There is no <code>\r</code>-and-overwrite progress bar and no cursor movement; <code>Cli::live</code> and <code>Cli::progress</code> hand the body a handle and paint nothing at all on a pipe</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path" title="Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal"><code>tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-terminal-profile-resolves-once" title="The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling"><code>tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output" title="There is no raw handle onto standard output or standard error, and no cursor, clipboard or title primitive"><code>tooling/no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-classes/running-a-statement/#db-transactions" title="A transaction is a closure, and Transaction is a Queryable rather than a second query surface"><code>core-classes/db-transactions</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided <div class="nv-rule" id="a-prompt-is-a-core-member">

## A prompt is a `Core\Cli` member that reads the controlling terminal, and `secret` originates a `secret`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-prompt-is-a-core-member"><code>tooling/a-prompt-is-a-core-member</code></a>
</div>

`Cli::ask`, `Cli::confirm`, `Cli::select<T>`, `Cli::multiSelect<T>` and `Cli::secret` are `Core`
members, because raw mode is unreachable from userland with the FFI door shut
([`security/no-ffi`](/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-ffi "No userland mechanism loads native code into the process")) and an extension runs in a sandbox with no tty: if `Core` does not ship the
interactive half, Novis does not have it at any tier. A question takes its options as one trailing
shape — `{default?, validate?}` on `ask`, `{default?}` on `confirm`, `{labels?, default?}` on
`select` — and a list of choices is `$choices`, since `options` is reserved for the trailing shape
([`core-api/options-bag`](/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/#options-bag "A member's optional knobs are one trailing shape literal, never a flag or a bitmask")).

Four properties follow from rules that already exist. `select<T>` returns the chosen value, not an
index. `confirm` returns a plain `bool`, because a closed two-case answer is a checked conversion and
a checked conversion launders. `secret` originates a `secret tainted string`
([`security/secret-has-no-ambient-source`](/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-has-no-ambient-source "Nothing grants secret ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract")), so a password typed at a prompt structurally cannot
be echoed, logged, dumped, put in a `Throwable` message or serialized. And **a prompt reads the
controlling terminal, not standard input** — `/dev/tty`, `CONIN$` — so `cat data.csv | myprog` can
still ask a question; without that, piping and prompting are mutually exclusive, which is the defect
in every hand-rolled version.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>readline()</code> reads standard input; <code>Cli::ask</code> reads the controlling terminal, so a piped program can still ask a question</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#a-prompt-never-blocks" title="A prompt never blocks: no terminal or no answer in five minutes takes the default or throws Cli\NotInteractive"><code>tooling/a-prompt-never-blocks</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-qualifier" title="secret is a second, independent compile-time qualifier, written before tainted and in that order alone"><code>security/secret-qualifier</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/secrets/#secret-has-no-ambient-source" title="Nothing grants secret ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract"><code>security/secret-has-no-ambient-source</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/closed-doors/#no-ffi" title="No userland mechanism loads native code into the process"><code>security/no-ffi</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-api/parameters-and-options/#options-bag" title="A member's optional knobs are one trailing shape literal, never a flag or a bitmask"><code>core-api/options-bag</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0033.md">record 0033</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0024.md">record 0024</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0052.md">record 0052</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-secret-originates-a-secret-no-sink-will-write.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-secret-originates-a-secret-no-sink-will-write.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-multiselect-answers-a-set-and-has-no-default.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-multiselect-answers-a-set-and-has-no-default.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-prompt-defaults-are-answered-whatever-shape-they-take.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-prompt-defaults-are-answered-whatever-shape-they-take.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="a-prompt-never-blocks">

## A prompt never blocks: no terminal or no answer in five minutes takes the `default` or throws `Cli\NotInteractive`

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-prompt-never-blocks"><code>tooling/a-prompt-never-blocks</code></a>
</div>

With no controlling terminal, a prompt returns its `default` if one was given and otherwise throws
`Cli\NotInteractive`. **It never blocks.** A CLI that hangs in CI waiting for an answer nobody can
give is the same failure as an outbound request with no deadline, and there is no spelling for an
unbounded wait.

A terminal that is there and unattended is the same rule, so the read is under a deadline too — five
minutes, after which the prompt takes the same `default` or throws the same class with a sentence
naming the deadline rather than a missing device. A CI job that allocated a pty, or a `docker run -t`
with no keyboard behind it, has a terminal by every test a process can make, and a blocking read there
would hang as long as the pipeline's own timeout allows. **No parameter lengthens it**, on any of the
five members: a `timeout` option would be the spelling for an unbounded wait, and a person who walks
away mid-answer getting a throw is priced at [`programs/memory-priority`](/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#memory-priority "Memory buys security, correctness, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated")'s ordering, where a
program that cannot hang outranks one that never gives up.

Under `nvs test`, prompts drain a scripted answer queue instead of reading a terminal:
`Core\Test::scriptAnswers(array<string> $answers)` — a member on the class the *test* calls, never a
filler on `Core\Cli` that would let production code answer its own prompts. It is drained where all
five prompts already meet, so a sixth inherits it. A scripted line wins over a terminal that is there,
and a queue with nothing left is the unattended run above, so scripting too few answers is assertable
rather than a hang.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>readline()</code> in CI hangs until the pipeline kills it; here it throws, and no <code>timeout</code> option lengthens the wait</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#a-prompt-is-a-core-member" title="A prompt is a Core\Cli member that reads the controlling terminal, and secret originates a secret"><code>tooling/a-prompt-is-a-core-member</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#memory-priority" title="Memory buys security, correctness, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated"><code>programs/memory-priority</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/testing/writing-a-test/#test-attribute" title="A test is a method marked #[Test], and its table is built while compiling"><code>testing/test-attribute</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0074.md">record 0074</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0079.md">record 0079</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-prompts-are-not-interactive-without-a-terminal.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-prompts-are-not-interactive-without-a-terminal.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/cli-a-prompt-with-no-default-throws-rather-than-waiting.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/cli-a-prompt-with-no-default-throws-rather-than-waiting.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/test-script-answers-drain-into-every-prompt.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/test-script-answers-drain-into-every-prompt.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path">

## Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path"><code>tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path</code></a>
</div>

Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region must be undone on a throw, on a fatal, on an internal
panic and on a signal. Restoration is an obligation of [`errors/escalation-ladder`](/docs/rules/errors/the-escalation-ladder/#escalation-ladder "A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried"), not a
`finally` an author remembers: a ladder that protects the process while leaving the operator's shell
in raw mode has failed at the thing it exists for. This is the most-forgotten defect in
cross-platform terminal code, and it is the reason in-place output is scoped rather than free-form
([`tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region "In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive")) — a region has an end, and the runtime is at
that end on every path.

A statement after the body cannot discharge the obligation, because a throw skips it and a panic
skips every statement there is ([`errors/panics-bypass-user-code`](/docs/rules/errors/the-escalation-ladder/#panics-bypass-user-code "An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code")). So the end of a region is a
destructor, in the stdlib's scope guard and in the runtime's region both — one ends the *scope*, the
other puts the *terminal* back — and an outer region closing also closes any inner one whose own
guard was skipped, so the stack can never keep a region nobody can reach. What is left on screen is
the last frame; what is restored is the cursor, and the row below the region is where the next `echo`
lands.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>A script that dies mid-prompt does not leave the shell in raw mode; restoration is the runtime's obligation rather than a <code>finally</code> the author remembers</p>
</aside>

<dl class="nv-rule-meta"><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>See also</dt><dd><a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region" title="In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive"><code>tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task" title="The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program, so a Core\Cli member throws in a request and in a spawned isolate"><code>tooling/the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/errors/the-escalation-ladder/#escalation-ladder" title="A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried"><code>errors/escalation-ladder</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/errors/the-escalation-ladder/#panics-bypass-user-code" title="An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code"><code>errors/panics-bypass-user-code</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/errors/the-escalation-ladder/#engine-floor" title="Tier 4 — the floor is native, bounded, and gives up rather than escalating"><code>errors/engine-floor</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided in</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0086.md">record 0086</a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/docs/decisions/0020.md">record 0020</a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Guarded by</dt><dd><a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cli.rs"><code>crates/nvs-stdlib/src/cli.rs</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/a-progress-bar-nests-inside-a-live-region.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/a-progress-bar-nests-inside-a-live-region.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="commands-are-compiled">

## `#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, and a duplicate name or an unbindable option fails the build

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#commands-are-compiled"><code>tooling/commands-are-compiled</code></a>
</div>

```nvs
#[Command(name: "deploy", about: "Push the current build")]
public static function deploy(
    string $target,
    #[Option(short: "n", about: "Print what would happen")] bool $dryRun,
    #[Option] uint $retries = 3,
): uint
```

`#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, over the same program enumeration
[`routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered`](/docs/rules/routing/declaring-a-route/#routes-are-compiled-not-registered "A route is a #[Route] compiled into the unit's table, and its three runtime bugs are compile errors") uses for the route table
([`programs/implementing`](/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#implementing "Core\Program::implementing<T>() lists every concrete class that is a T, for an interface or a class, and it expands while compiling")). The three errors every run-time argument parser discovers at the
worst moment are **compile errors** here: a duplicate command name, two options of one command sharing
a short or long spelling, and an `#[Option]` on a parameter whose declared type has no conversion from
`string`. A `#[Command]` method is static and returns `void` (exit status 0) or `uint`.

A program with no `#[Command]` builds no table, runs no scan and pays nothing. Nobody writes usage
text and nobody lets it rot, because help and completions are read off the table
([`tooling/command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated "Core\Command::run dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated from the table")). What each parameter becomes on the
command line is [`tooling/a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option`](/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option "A command parameter is a positional argument unless it carries #[Option], and its type converts and launders the word"). The alternative — a
`clap`-shaped builder registered at run time — loses all three compile errors and the generated
completions, and is the design every other ecosystem already has.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p><code>getopt()</code> and hand-parsed <code>$argv</code> become a table built while compiling; a duplicate command, two options sharing a spelling, or an <code>#[Option]</code> on a type no text converts into is a compile error rather than a run-time surprise</p>
</aside>

a positional argument unless it carries #[Option], and its type converts and launders the word"><code>tooling/a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/tooling/the-terminal/#command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated" title="Core\Command::run dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated <div class="nv-rule" id="a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option">

## A command parameter is a positional argument unless it carries `#[Option]`, and its type converts and launders the word

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option"><code>tooling/a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option</code></a>
</div>

**A parameter is a positional argument unless it carries `#[Option]`.** One sentence, with no
inference from defaults or types. A `bool` `#[Option]` is a flag; a trailing `array<string>` parameter
is variadic. An argument the command line leaves out takes the parameter's declared default, so
`#[Option] uint $retries = 3` is optional and a parameter declaring none is required — the flag being
the one exception, since being *written* is how it is given, and an unwritten `bool $loud = true` is
still `false`. Nothing new is admitted: a default is already a literal of the parameter's own type, so
the table carries the folded constant as the text a command line would have written and the matcher
converts it exactly as it converts a written word.

**A matched value's type comes from the parameter.** `uint $retries` is converted during matching
and, because a checked conversion launders ([`security/route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type`](/docs/rules/security/laundering/#route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type "A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a string capture stays tainted")),
arrives **unqualified**; `string $target` arrives `tainted`. An enum converts by its case name, a
union of literals by its word ([`routing/a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set`](/docs/rules/routing/declaring-a-route/#a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set "A capture narrows to a closed set with a literal-union or enum-subset type, never with a regex")), and a non-numeric
`--retries` is a usage error rather than a crash. This is the route capture's rule applied unchanged
— no new laundering rule exists for the command line. An `#[Option]` written outside a `#[Command]`
method supplies nothing, because there is no table for it to be a row of.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>An argument arrives as the parameter's declared type, <code>uint</code> unqualified and <code>string</code> <code>tainted</code>, instead of every option being a string in an array</p>
</aside>

compiling, and a duplicate name or an unbindable option fails the build"><code>tooling/commands-are-compiled</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/security/laundering/#route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type" title="A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a string capture stays tainted"><code>security/route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/routing/declaring-a-route/#a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set" title="A capture narrows to a closed set with a literal-union or enum-subset type, never with a regex"><code>routing/a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set</code></a> <a href="/docs/rules/core-classes/processes-and-files/#cli-arguments" title="Core\Cli::arguments is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth"><code>core-classes/cli-arguments</code></a></dd></div><div class="nv-rule-meta-row"><dt>Decided href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/core/command-run-throws-for-a-parameter-no-argument-converts-into.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/core/command-run-throws-for-a-parameter-no-argument-converts-into.nvst</code></a> <a href="https://github.com/novis-lang/novis/blob/main/tests/conformance/reject/an-option-marker-outside-a-command-method-supplies-nothing.nvst"><code>tests/conformance/reject/an-option-marker-outside-a-command-method-supplies-nothing.nvst</code></a></dd></div></dl>

</div>

<div class="nv-rule" id="command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated">

## `Core\Command::run` dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated from the table

<div class="nv-rule-tags">
<span class="nv-rule-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span>
<span class="nv-rule-flag">Differs from PHP</span>
<a class="nv-rule-id" href="#command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated"><code>tooling/command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated</code></a>
</div>

`Core\Command::run(): uint` is the entry point: it matches the command line against the compiled
table, dispatches to the handler the first word names, and returns the process exit status — a
handler's `void` is `0`, and `exit` still works from inside one
([`statements/exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword`](/docs/rules/statements/by-reference-and-exit/#exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword "exit is the only process-termination keyword; die is refused")). A command line the table cannot fill is a
usage error — the usage line and a non-zero status — not a crash.

`Core\Command::help(?string $name): Cli\Text` and `Core\Command::completions(Cli\Shell $shell): string`
are generated from the same table, for `bash`, `zsh`, `fish` and `pwsh` — the four cases of
`Cli\Shell`, and nothing else. Two artefacts read one table, so neither can disagree with the program.

This is the **one deliberate divergence** from the route table: [`routing/matching-is-not-dispatching`](/docs/rules/routing/matching/#matching-is-not-dispatching "The router stops at matching: a match is a name and typed parameters, and nothing here dispatches")
stops at matching because a web framework must own the pipeline — middleware, controllers, response
mapping — and baking a convention in would fight it. A CLI has one entry point and no middleware
question, so the reason the router stops does not exist here, and stopping anyway would copy its
shape rather than its reasoning.

<aside class="nv-rule-diverges">
<p class="nv-rule-diverges-label">Where this differs from PHP</p>
<p>Nobody writes a usage block or a completion script; <code>--help</code> and <code>bash</code>/<code>zsh</code>/<code>fish</code>/<code>pwsh</code> completions are read off the compiled table</p>
</aside>

</div>
